lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.d: Joshua records Israel crossing the Jordan after Moses' death (1:1-2), taking and dividing the land, and Joshua's closing call to serve the LORD at Shechem, ending with his death (24:29).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline the book of Joshua from the crossing of the Jordan to the covenant at Shechem?
ev: Say how the book begins with the death of Moses and ends with the death of Joshua
Name the three parts: entering and conquering, dividing the land, and the farewell charges

nodes.d: After Moses dies, the LORD tells Joshua to lead the people over the Jordan, promises to be with him, and charges him to keep the law; Joshua then orders the people to prepare and the eastern tribes pledge their help.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God said to Joshua at the start of the book?
ev: Retell what the LORD told Joshua after Moses died
Say what Joshua was told to do with the book of the law (1:7-8)
Explain what Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh promised (1:12-18)

nodes.t: Rahab hides the spies in Jericho
nodes.d: Joshua sends two men to Jericho, where Rahab hides them, confesses that the LORD is God in heaven and earth, and secures their oath to spare her family, marked by a scarlet cord.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Rahab did for the spies and what they promised her?
ev: Retell how Rahab hid the spies
Say what Rahab had heard about the LORD (2:9-11)
Describe the promise the men made and the sign of the scarlet line (2:12-21)

nodes.d: The priests carry the ark into the Jordan, its waters are cut off, and Israel crosses on dry ground; twelve stones are taken from the river as a memorial for children to ask about.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israel crossed the Jordan and why the stones were set up?
ev: Retell how Israel crossed the Jordan
Explain what the twelve stones were for (4:6-7, 4:21-24)
Say what Joshua 4:23 compares the crossing to

nodes.t: Circumcision, Passover and the captain of the LORD's host
nodes.d: At Gilgal the new generation is circumcised, Israel keeps the passover and eats the produce of the land as the manna ceases, and Joshua meets the captain of the LORD's host near Jericho.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what happened at Gilgal before Jericho?
ev: Explain why Joshua circumcised the people (5:4-7)
Say what happened to the manna (5:12)
Describe Joshua's meeting by Jericho and what he was told to do (5:13-15)

nodes.d: Israel marches round Jericho for seven days with the ark and trumpets, the wall falls at the shout, the city is devoted to destruction, and Rahab and her household are saved.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Jericho fell and who was saved?
ev: Retell the instructions for marching round Jericho (6:3-5)
Say what happened on the seventh day (6:15-20)
Explain why Rahab and her household were spared (6:22-25)

nodes.t: Achan's sin and defeat at Ai
nodes.d: Israel is routed at Ai because Achan took devoted things from Jericho; Joshua prays, the LORD reveals the sin by lot, and Achan confesses and is stoned.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Israel was defeated at Ai?
ev: Retell why Israel lost at Ai (7:1, 7:10-12)
Describe how Achan was found out and what he confessed (7:16-21)
Say what the LORD calls the people's act in 7:11

nodes.d: The LORD tells Joshua not to fear and to ambush Ai; the city is drawn out, burned, and taken, and Israel may take its spoil.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Israel took Ai the second time?
ev: Retell the ambush plan and how it worked
Say how this differs from Jericho regarding spoil (8:2)

nodes.t: The law read at Mount Ebal
nodes.d: Joshua builds an altar on Mount Ebal as Moses commanded, writes a copy of the law on stones, and reads all its blessings and cursings to the whole assembly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Israel did at Mount Ebal after Ai?
ev: Say what Joshua built and wrote on Mount Ebal
Explain who heard the law read (8:33-35)

nodes.d: The people of Gibeon pretend to come from a far country and trick Israel into a treaty without asking the LORD; when found out, they are made woodcutters and water carriers and spared because of the oath.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Gibeonites tricked Joshua and what happened next?
ev: Retell how Gibeon deceived Israel
Say what Israel failed to do (9:14)
Explain why Israel did not destroy them (9:18-21)

nodes.d: Five Amorite kings attack Gibeon; Joshua marches all night, the LORD sends hailstones, the sun stands still at Joshua's word, and the five kings are caught in a cave at Makkedah and put to death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened when the five kings attacked Gibeon?
ev: Say why Israel went to help Gibeon
Describe what the LORD did in the battle (10:10-14)
Say what happened to the five kings (10:16-27)

nodes.d: Joshua takes Makkedah, Libnah, Lachish, Eglon, Hebron and Debir and the surrounding country, because the LORD God of Israel fought for Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some cities Joshua took in the south and say who gave the victory?
ev: List some of the southern cities Joshua took
Say who fought for Israel (10:42)

nodes.t: The northern campaign and the whole land taken
nodes.d: Jabin of Hazor gathers northern kings at the waters of Merom; the LORD delivers them to Israel, Hazor is burned, and the summary says Joshua took the land according to what the LORD told Moses and the land rested from war.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell about the battle at Merom and the summary of Joshua's conquest?
ev: Say who gathered at Merom and what the LORD told Joshua
Explain what chapter 11 says about Gibeon being the only city to make peace (11:19)
Say how the chapter says Joshua obeyed Moses' commands (11:15)

nodes.d: Joshua 12 lists the two kings Moses defeated east of the Jordan and thirty-one kings Joshua defeated to the west.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the list in Joshua 12 shows?
ev: Name Sihon and Og as the kings on the east side (12:1-6)
Say how many kings are listed west of the Jordan (12:24)

nodes.t: Land still to be possessed and the eastern tribes
nodes.d: The LORD tells the aged Joshua that much land remains and orders it divided; the chapter recalls Moses' gifts east of the Jordan to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh, and that the Levites' inheritance was the LORD himself.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Joshua 13 says remained and who already had land?
ev: Say what the LORD told old Joshua (13:1, 13:6-7)
Name the tribes that received land from Moses east of the Jordan
Say what the Levites' inheritance was (13:14, 13:33)

nodes.d: Caleb recalls Moses' oath at Kadesh and, at eighty-five, asks for the hill country of Hebron; Joshua blesses him, Caleb drives out the sons of Anak, and Othniel wins Debir and Achsah.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Caleb received Hebron?
ev: Say why Caleb says he deserves Hebron (14:8-9)
Retell how Othniel won Achsah (15:16-17)

nodes.d: The lot for Judah is described by its borders and cities, and the text notes that Judah could not drive out the Jebusites from Jerusalem.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what Joshua 15 describes and what Judah failed to do?
ev: Say what chapter 15 says about the Jebusites in Jerusalem (15:63)

nodes.d: The lots for Ephraim and Manasseh are described, the daughters of Zelophehad receive their inheritance, Canaanites in Gezer remain, and the house of Joseph complains of too little land and is told to clear the hill country.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ephraim and Manasseh received and what they were told to do?
ev: Name the two tribes of the house of Joseph
Say what Zelophehad's daughters asked for (17:3-4)
Say what Joshua told the house of Joseph to do (17:14-18)

nodes.t: Shiloh and the seven remaining tribes
nodes.d: Israel sets up the tabernacle at Shiloh; Joshua rebukes the seven tribes for delaying, sends men to describe the land in seven parts, and casts lots for Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan before receiving his own city.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the last seven tribes got their land?
ev: Say what Joshua told the seven tribes (18:3)
List the remaining tribes who received lots
Say what city Joshua received (19:49-50)

nodes.d: The LORD tells Joshua to appoint cities of refuge where someone who killed unwittingly can flee from the avenger of blood; six cities are named, three on each side of the Jordan.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what a city of refuge was for?
ev: Say who could flee to a city of refuge and who could not be handed over to the avenger (20:3-5)
Name some of the six cities (20:7-8)

nodes.t: Cities for the Levites and the promises kept
nodes.d: The Levites receive forty-eight cities from the tribes by lot, and the chapter ends by saying the LORD gave Israel all the land he swore to their fathers, gave them rest, and not one good word failed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Joshua 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises?
ev: Say why the Levites got cities rather than a tribal territory (21:2)
Say what 21:43-45 says about the LORD's promises

nodes.d: Joshua sends the eastern tribes home; they build a great altar by the Jordan, the western tribes prepare for war, and Phinehas and ten princes confront them, learning that the altar is a witness and not for sacrifice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the story of the altar by the Jordan and how Israel avoided war?
ev: Say why the western tribes were alarmed (22:11-20)
Explain what the eastern tribes said the altar was for (22:24-29)
Say how the dispute ended and what the altar was named (22:30-34)

nodes.d: Old Joshua calls Israel to keep the law, cling to the LORD and avoid the remaining nations, warning that if they turn away and break the covenant, the LORD will bring evil on them.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Joshua's warning in chapter 23?
ev: Say what Joshua told Israel to cling to
Say what Joshua warned would happen if they served other gods (23:12-16)

nodes.t: Choose this day: the covenant at Shechem
nodes.d: At Shechem Joshua recounts God's acts from Abraham to the conquest, urges Israel to choose whom to serve, makes a covenant with the people, and sets up a stone of witness before dying at 110.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Shechem and what Joshua said about choosing whom to serve?
ev: Say what Joshua and his house decided (24:15)
Retell the history Joshua recounted (24:2-13)
Say what Joshua did that day and where he was buried (24:25-30)

nodes.d: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God promised Abram in Genesis 12:1-3?
ev: State the promises of 12:1-3
Say that Abram went as the LORD told him

nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.d: Judges tells of Israel after Joshua's death, repeatedly falling into idolatry, being oppressed, crying out and being delivered by judges, and ends with the refrain that there was no king in Israel and everyone did what was right in his own eyes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the cycle of sin, oppression, crying out and deliverance in Judges?
ev: Describe the repeating pattern in Judges 2:11-19
Name several judges and the enemies they faced
Say what 21:25 says about Israel at the end

nodes.t: Judah's victories and tribes that failed to drive out the Canaanites
nodes.d: After Joshua's death Judah and Simeon fight first, Othniel wins Achsah, and the chapter lists tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants; the angel of the LORD at Bochim says this disobedience will leave the nations as snares.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened after Joshua died and why the angel spoke at Bochim?
ev: Say who went up first against the Canaanites (1:1-2)
Name some tribes that did not drive out the inhabitants (1:27-33)
Say what the angel of the LORD said and how the people responded (2:1-5)

nodes.d: After Joshua's generation a new generation forgets the LORD and serves Baal; he gives them to enemies, raises up judges to deliver them, and leaves nations to test Israel, who also intermarry and serve their gods.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the pattern that repeats through the book of Judges?
ev: Retell the pattern in 2:11-19
Say why the LORD left nations in the land (2:20-22, 3:1-4)

nodes.d: A three-year famine comes, and the LORD says it is because Saul put the Gibeonites to death; at the Gibeonites' request seven of Saul's sons are hanged, Mephibosheth is spared for the sake of the oath with Jonathan, and Saul's and Jonathan's bones are buried in Kish's tomb.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the famine came and what David did about it?
ev: Say what the LORD said was the cause of the famine (21:1)
Say why Mephibosheth was spared (21:7)
Say what David did with the bones of Saul and Jonathan (21:12-14)

nodes.t: By faith Moses, Israel and Rahab
nodes.d: By faith Moses' parents hid him, Moses chose affliction with God's people over Egypt's pleasures, kept the Passover, Israel crossed the Red Sea and the walls of Jericho fell, and Rahab was not destroyed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what Moses chose by faith and why (11:24-27)?
ev: List what Moses did by faith (11:24-28)
Name the two events of 11:29-30

nodes.d: The writer calls for brotherly love and hospitality to strangers, remembering prisoners, honour in marriage, and a life free from covetousness because God has said he will never leave or forsake.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name some practical commands in 13:1-5 and the promise that supports them?
ev: List the commands of 13:1-5
Say what promise supports contentment (13:5)

nodes.d: The letter to the Hebrews presents Jesus as God's Son, greater than angels and Moses, our great high priest after Melchizedek who mediates a better covenant by one sacrifice, and calls readers to faith and endurance.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain in a few sentences what Hebrews teaches about Jesus and what the readers are told to do?
ev: Describe the main parts: the Son (1-2), Moses and rest (3-4), the high priest (4-7), the new covenant and sacrifice (8-10), faith (11), endurance and exhortations (12-13)

nodes.d: James is a letter from James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, with practical teaching on trials, living faith, the tongue, humility, wealth and patience.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what James tells believers to do with trials, words and wealth?
ev: Name the main themes of James in order
Say who the letter is from and to whom it is written

nodes.d: James argues that faith without works is dead, using the demons who believe, Abraham offering Isaac, and Rahab, and concludes a man is justified by works and not by faith only.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what James is arguing about the kind of faith that is dead?
ev: Explain what James means by faith that is alone and dead
Retell how Abraham and Rahab are used as examples
Compare the wording of James 2:24 with Romans 3:28 and 4:2-3
